findings.quoted_finding: Strüver (2016) explicitly argues that economic interests and trade cause diplomatic affinity and therefore contradicts the manuscript's reverse-causality concern.
source_locations: Strüver GIGA Working Paper 209/2012:physical page 21 (printed 20), physical page 23 (printed 22), physical page 24 (printed 23)
Oxford Academic final publication record and abstract, accessed 2026-09-14: https://academic.oup.com/fpa/article-abstract/12/2/170/2367626
refuting_evidence: The official abstract reports exploratory logistic regressions and correlations, not a trade-identified causal effect.
The relevant results distinguish trade dependence from aid and arms and indicate that trade dependence is more plausibly a consequence that helps maintain similarity than a prerequisite for onset.
The discussion says political understanding is conducive to economic exchange, which is compatible with the manuscript's reverse-causality concern.
The conclusion explicitly says no causal link between foreign-policy similarity and the explanatory factors has been established.

findings.reasoning: The reviewer conflates the article's theoretical mechanisms and observed associations with causal identification. Strüver does not demonstrate the claimed trade-to-alignment causal direction and explicitly discusses the reverse direction that motivates the manuscript's concern.
findings.proposed_fix_detail: Do not rewrite the sentence to claim that Strüver establishes trade as the primary cause of diplomatic alignment.
findings.disposition: Retain the sentence and Strüver citation; no replacement.

findings.quoted_finding: MacDonald and Parent (2021) reject the relational definition and state in their abstract that status is an attribute, not a relation, so their inclusion is a material misattribution.
source_locations: Cambridge University Press publication record and abstract, accessed 2026-09-14: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/world-politics/article/abs/status-of-status-in-world-politics/BF85C05AAB728662D3CA526CDF69DA60
Author-affiliated Notre Dame conceptual summary, accessed 2026-09-14: https://ondisc.nd.edu/news-media/news/the-status-of-status-in-world-politics/
Paul K. MacDonald publication list, accessed 2026-09-14: https://sites.google.com/a/wellesley.edu/paul-k-macdonald/publications
defect_evidence: The compact citation cluster can be read as presenting MacDonald and Parent as unqualified proponents of the manuscript's definition.
The official abstract instead frames the article as a critical stocktaking and says the consensus definition conceals tensions between standing and membership.
refuting_evidence: The two phrases attributed to the abstract by the reviewer do not appear in the official publisher abstract.
The publisher abstract and author-affiliated summary identify the dispute as standing versus membership, not attribute versus relation.
The source discusses valued attributes, positions, and rights and responsibilities; it does not supply the categorical rejection alleged by the reviewer.
The BibTeX title, authors, year, journal, volume, issue, pages, and DOI 10.1017/S0043887120000301 match the publisher record.

findings.reasoning: The review's evidence and strong theoretical characterization are false, but its narrower citation-fidelity concern is valid: a critical review should not be left inside an undifferentiated cluster that may imply endorsement. Removing only the citation preserves the author's relational definition without importing the reviewer's fabricated opposition.
